stem: In the figure, lines ℓ and m are parallel. What is the value of x?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><line x1="20" y1="60" x2="280" y2="60" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="20" y1="160" x2="280" y2="160" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="177.8" y1="15.7" x2="144.6" y2="204.3" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><text x="272" y="52" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">ℓ</text><text x="272" y="152" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">m</text><text x="191.9" y="91" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">4x°</text><text x="210.4" y="144" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">(2x + 30)°</text></svg>
explanation: Both labeled angles lie between the parallel lines on the same side of the transversal, so they are same-side interior angles and add up to 180°. Then 4x + (2x + 30) = 180, so 6x = 150 and x = 25. Setting the two angles equal, as if they were alternate interior angles, gives 2x = 30 and the trap answer 15.

stem:
One angle of an isosceles triangle measures 40°. Which of the following could be the measure, in degrees, of another angle of the triangle?

Indicate all such measures.
explanation: There are two cases. If 40° is the vertex angle, the two base angles are (180 − 40)/2 = 70° each. If 40° is a base angle, the other base angle is also 40° and the vertex angle is 180 − 80 = 100°. So another angle can be 40, 70 or 100. 110 and 140 come from subtracting 40 or 70 from 180 and forgetting the third angle.

stem: What is the perimeter of the right triangle shown?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><polygon points="60,185 240,185 60,50" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><polyline points="70,185 70,175 60,175" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><text x="150" y="207" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">12</text><text x="44" y="122" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">9</text></svg>
explanation: By the Pythagorean theorem the hypotenuse is √(9² + 12²) = √225 = 15 (a 3-4-5 triangle scaled by 3). The perimeter is 9 + 12 + 15 = 36. The choice 54 is the area, ½ × 9 × 12, and 21 leaves out the hypotenuse.

stem: Each interior angle of a regular polygon measures 150°. How many sides does the polygon have?
explanation: Each exterior angle is 180° − 150° = 30°, and the exterior angles of any polygon add up to 360°, so there are 360/30 = 12 sides. Check: a 12-gon has interior angle sum (12 − 2) × 180 = 1,800°, and 1,800/12 = 150°.

stem: In the figure, one side of the triangle is extended. What is the value of x?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><polygon points="82.9,14.9 40,175 195,175" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><line x1="195" y1="175" x2="280" y2="175" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><text x="90.2" y="61.3" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">50°</text><text x="60.6" y="164.2" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">x°</text><text x="208.9" y="153.4" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">125°</text></svg>
explanation: An exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles, so 125 = 50 + x and x = 75. Alternatively, the interior angle next to the 125° angle is 55°, and 180 − 50 − 55 = 75. The choice 55 is that interior angle, not x.

stem: A rectangle has a perimeter of 46 and a diagonal of length 17. What is the area of the rectangle?
explanation: Let the sides be l and w. Then l + w = 23 and l² + w² = 17² = 289. Since (l + w)² = l² + w² + 2lw, 529 = 289 + 2lw, so lw = 120 (the sides are 8 and 15). 240 is 2lw, and 132.25 assumes the rectangle is a square with side 11.5, which would give a diagonal of about 16.3, not 17.

stem: In triangle ABC, segment DE is parallel to BC, AD = 4, DB = 6 and DE = 5. What is the length of BC?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><polygon points="150,25 35,195 265,195" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><line x1="104" y1="93" x2="196" y2="93" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><text x="150" y="19" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">A</text><text x="25" y="203" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">B</text><text x="275" y="203" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">C</text><text x="90" y="97" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">D</text><text x="210" y="97" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">E</text><text x="113" y="61" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">4</text><text x="55.5" y="146" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">6</text><text x="150" y="85" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">5</text></svg>
explanation: Because DE ∥ BC, triangle ADE is similar to triangle ABC with ratio AD/AB = 4/(4 + 6) = 4/10. So DE/BC = 4/10, giving BC = 5 × 10/4 = 12.5. The trap 7.5 uses DB instead of the whole side AB (5 × 6/4); corresponding sides must both be measured from A.

stem: The hypotenuse of a 30°-60°-90° triangle has length 10. What is the area of the triangle?
explanation: In a 30°-60°-90° triangle the sides are in the ratio 1 : √3 : 2, so the legs are 5 and 5√3. The area is ½ × 5 × 5√3 = 25√3/2 ≈ 21.7. The choice 25√3 forgets the ½, and 25 multiplies the short leg by the hypotenuse, which is not a height.

stem: The measures of the four angles of a quadrilateral are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4 : 6. What is the measure, in degrees, of the largest angle?
explanation: The angles of a quadrilateral add up to 360°. The ratio has 2 + 3 + 4 + 6 = 15 parts, so one part is 360/15 = 24° and the largest angle is 6 × 24 = 144°. Using 180° (the triangle sum) by mistake would give 72.

stem: Two sides of a triangle have lengths 7 and 11. If the third side has an integer length, how many different lengths are possible for the third side?
explanation: The third side must be greater than 11 − 7 = 4 and less than 11 + 7 = 18, so it can be 5, 6, ..., 17. That is 17 − 5 + 1 = 13 values. 14 wrongly includes 4 (sides 4, 7, 11 would lie flat), and 12 forgets to add 1 when counting the integers from 5 to 17.

stem: ABCD is a square with side length 8, and E is the midpoint of side BC. What is the area of the shaded region AECD?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><polygon points="70,30 230,110 230,190 70,190" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="#dddddd"/><polygon points="70,30 230,30 230,190 70,190" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><text x="58" y="34" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">A</text><text x="242" y="34" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">B</text><text x="242" y="198" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">C</text><text x="58" y="198" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">D</text><text x="242" y="116" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">E</text><text x="150" y="22" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">8</text></svg>
explanation: The unshaded part is right triangle ABE with legs AB = 8 and BE = 4, so its area is ½ × 8 × 4 = 16. The shaded region is the square minus this triangle: 64 − 16 = 48. The choice 16 is the triangle itself, and 32 treats AE as cutting the square in half.

stem:
Which of the following could be the lengths of the three sides of a triangle?

Indicate all such sets of lengths.
explanation: Three lengths form a triangle exactly when the two shorter ones add up to more than the longest. 4 + 5 = 9 > 8, 3 + 7 = 10 > 9 and 1.5 + 2 = 3.5 > 3 all work. 2 + 3 = 5 < 6 fails, and 5 + 5 = 10 is not greater than 10, so those segments would lie flat in a line; equality is not enough.

stem: What is the area of the parallelogram shown?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><polygon points="40,175 200,175 283.1,127 123.1,127" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><text x="120" y="198" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">10</text><text x="67.6" y="141" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">6</text><text x="102" y="169" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">30°</text></svg>
explanation: Drop a height from the top left vertex to the base of length 10. It cuts off a 30°-60°-90° triangle whose hypotenuse is the side of length 6, so the height (opposite the 30° angle) is 3. Area = base × height = 10 × 3 = 30. 60 multiplies the two sides, which is right only for a rectangle; 30√3 uses the longer leg 3√3 as the height.

stem: An isosceles right triangle has an area of 18. What is its perimeter?
explanation: If each leg is a, the area is a²/2 = 18, so a = 6. The hypotenuse of an isosceles right triangle is a√2 = 6√2, so the perimeter is 6 + 6 + 6√2 = 12 + 6√2. The choice 18 treats the triangle as equilateral with side 6, and 6 + 6√2 counts only one leg.

stem: In the figure, three lines meet at a point. What is the value of 2x?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><line x1="280" y1="112" x2="20" y2="112" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="245.8" y1="31.7" x2="54.2" y2="192.3" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="97.5" y1="21.1" x2="202.5" y2="202.9" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><text x="198.9" y="94.2" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">x°</text><text x="156.9" y="72.6" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">2x°</text><text x="189.8" y="135" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">60°</text></svg>
explanation: The 60° angle below the horizontal line is vertical to the angle above it on the left, so that angle is also 60°. The three angles above the horizontal line form a straight angle: x + 2x + 60 = 180, so x = 40 and 2x = 80. The choice 40 is x, not 2x.

stem: What is the area of the isosceles trapezoid shown?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><polygon points="30,180 270,180 206,132 94,132" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><text x="150" y="202" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">15</text><text x="150" y="124" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">7</text><text x="50" y="156" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">5</text><text x="250" y="156" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">5</text></svg>
explanation: Drop heights from the ends of the shorter base. They cut off two right triangles, each with a horizontal leg of (15 − 7)/2 = 4 and a hypotenuse of 5, so the height is 3 (a 3-4-5 triangle). Area = ½ × (7 + 15) × 3 = 33. The choice 55 uses the slanted side 5 as the height; a height must be perpendicular to the bases.

stem: The sum of the measures of the interior angles of a convex polygon is 1,980°. How many sides does the polygon have?
explanation: A polygon with n sides has interior angle sum (n − 2) × 180°. Setting (n − 2) × 180 = 1,980 gives n − 2 = 11, so n = 13. A common slip is to stop at 11, which is the number of triangles the polygon splits into, not the number of sides.

stem: In triangle ABC, the measure of angle A is twice the measure of angle B, and the measure of angle C is 20° greater than the measure of angle B. What is the measure of angle A?
explanation: Write every angle in terms of angle B = b: A = 2b and C = b + 20. Then 2b + b + b + 20 = 180, so 4b = 160 and b = 40. Angle A is 2 × 40 = 80°. The choice 40° is angle B and 60° is angle C; read which angle the question asks for.

stem: A 13-foot ladder leans against a vertical wall with its foot 5 feet from the base of the wall, as shown. If the foot of the ladder is pulled straight away from the wall until it is 12 feet from the wall, how many feet does the top of the ladder slide down?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><line x1="230" y1="20" x2="230" y2="195" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="30" y1="195" x2="270" y2="195" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="162.5" y1="195" x2="230" y2="33" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><polyline points="230,185 220,185 220,195" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><text x="182.2" y="110" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">13</text><text x="196.2" y="215" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">5</text></svg>
explanation: At first the top is √(13² − 5²) = 12 feet up the wall. After the move the foot is 12 feet out, so the top is √(13² − 12²) = 5 feet up. The top slides down 12 − 5 = 7 feet. Answering 7 because the foot moved 7 feet is a coincidence of this 5-12-13 triangle, not a rule; in general the two distances differ.

stem:
A rectangle has an area of 36, and the length of each of its sides is an integer. Which of the following could be the perimeter of the rectangle?

Indicate all such perimeters.
explanation: The side pairs with product 36 are 1 × 36, 2 × 18, 3 × 12, 4 × 9 and 6 × 6, giving perimeters 74, 40, 30, 26 and 24. A square is a rectangle, so 24 counts. No pair gives 48: that would need sides adding to 24 with product 36, which has no integer solution.

stem: In triangle ABC, the measure of angle A is 70°. The bisectors of angles B and C meet at point P, as shown. What is the measure of angle BPC?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><polygon points="127.8,20.6 30,190 270,190" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><line x1="30" y1="190" x2="137.2" y2="128.1" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="270" y1="190" x2="137.2" y2="128.1" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><text x="127.8" y="14.6" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">A</text><text x="20" y="198" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">B</text><text x="280" y="198" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">C</text><text x="137.2" y="118.1" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">P</text><text x="130.8" y="59.4" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">70°</text></svg>
explanation: Angles B and C add up to 180 − 70 = 110°. Each bisector takes half of its angle, so in triangle BPC the angles at B and C add up to 110/2 = 55°. Then angle BPC = 180 − 55 = 125°. The value does not depend on how the 110° is split between B and C. The choice 110° stops before halving, and 140° doubles angle A.

stem: A right triangle has a perimeter of 60 and a hypotenuse of length 25. What is the area of the triangle?
explanation: The legs a and b satisfy a + b = 35 and a² + b² = 625. Squaring the first, 1,225 = 625 + 2ab, so ab = 300 and the area is ab/2 = 150 (the legs are 15 and 20). The choice 300 is ab itself; the area of a right triangle is half the product of the legs.

stem: A triangle has sides of lengths 13, 14 and 15. What is the length of the altitude to the side of length 14?
explanation: Let the altitude h meet the side of length 14, splitting it into parts x and 14 − x. Then 13² − x² = h² = 15² − (14 − x)², which gives 169 − x² = 225 − 196 + 28x − x², so 28x = 140 and x = 5. Hence h = √(169 − 25) = 12. (Equivalently, the area is 84 and h = 2 × 84/14.) Guessing 13.5 or 14 by averaging sides ignores the right triangles.

stem: The figure shows a regular hexagon with sides of length 2. The shaded triangle is formed by joining three alternate vertices of the hexagon. What is the area of the shaded triangle?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><polygon points="150,18 70.3,64 70.3,156 150,202 229.7,156 229.7,64" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><polygon points="150,18 70.3,156 229.7,156" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="#dddddd"/><text x="189.8" y="201" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">2</text></svg>
explanation: Each side of the triangle cuts off an isosceles triangle with sides 2, 2 and a 120° angle between them; splitting it gives two 30°-60°-90° triangles, so the cut side is 2√3. The shaded triangle is equilateral with side 2√3, so its area is (√3/4) × (2√3)² = (√3/4) × 12 = 3√3. The choice 6√3 is the area of the whole hexagon; the shaded triangle is exactly half of it.

stem:
In triangle PQR, PQ = 6, QR = 10 and angle Q is obtuse. Which of the following could be the length of PR?

Indicate all such lengths.
explanation: If angle Q were exactly 90°, PR would be √(6² + 10²) = √136 ≈ 11.7. An obtuse angle at Q makes the opposite side longer, so PR > √136. The triangle inequality also requires PR < 6 + 10 = 16. So PR is between about 11.7 and 16: 12, 13 and 15 work. 11 would make Q acute, and 16 or 17 cannot form a triangle.

stem: The length of the diagonal of a square is increased by 50%. By what percent does the area of the square increase?
explanation: The side of a square is its diagonal divided by √2, so every length scales by the same factor 1.5 and the area scales by 1.5² = 2.25. That is an increase of 125%. The choice 50% assumes area grows like length, and 100% doubles the 50% instead of squaring the factor.

stem: In right triangle ABC, angle C is a right angle and CD is perpendicular to AB. If AD = 4 and DB = 9, what is the area of triangle ABC?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><polygon points="33,180 267,180 105,72" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><line x1="105" y1="72" x2="105" y2="180" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><polyline points="114,180 114,171 105,171" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><polyline points="99.5,80.3 107.8,85.9 113.3,77.5" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><text x="23" y="188" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">A</text><text x="277" y="188" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">B</text><text x="105" y="64" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">C</text><text x="105" y="200" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">D</text><text x="69" y="200" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">4</text><text x="186" y="200" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">9</text></svg>
explanation: The altitude to the hypotenuse creates two triangles similar to each other: ADC ~ CDB, so AD/CD = CD/DB and CD² = 4 × 9 = 36, giving CD = 6. The area of ABC is ½ × AB × CD = ½ × 13 × 6 = 39. The choice 78 forgets the ½, and 36 is CD², not an area.

stem: Each exterior angle of a regular polygon is one-fifth of each interior angle. How many diagonals does the polygon have?
explanation: An interior angle and its exterior angle add up to 180°. If the exterior angle is e, then e + 5e = 180, so e = 30° and the polygon has 360/30 = 12 sides. Each vertex joins to 12 − 3 = 9 non-adjacent vertices, and each diagonal is counted twice, so there are 12 × 9/2 = 54 diagonals. Forgetting to halve gives 108.

stem: The perimeter of a rhombus is 40, and the lengths of its diagonals are in the ratio 3 : 4. What is the area of the rhombus?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><polygon points="150,20 270,110 150,200 30,110" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><line x1="150" y1="20" x2="150" y2="200" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/><line x1="270" y1="110" x2="30" y2="110" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/></svg>
explanation: Each side is 40/4 = 10. The diagonals bisect each other at right angles, so half-diagonals 3k and 4k form a right triangle with hypotenuse 10: 5k = 10, k = 2. The diagonals are 12 and 16, and the area is 12 × 16/2 = 96. The choice 192 forgets to halve the product of the diagonals, and 100 treats the rhombus as a square.

stem: Two different isosceles triangles each have two sides of length 10 and an area of 48. What is the sum of the lengths of their third sides?
explanation: The height to the base b splits the triangle into two right triangles with hypotenuse 10 and legs b/2 and h, where (b/2) × h = 48 and (b/2)² + h² = 100. The pairs (6, 8) and (8, 6) both work, so b = 12 (height 8) or b = 16 (height 6). Their sum is 28. Choosing 12 or 16 alone misses the second triangle.

stem: In triangle PQR, point S lies on side QR, and PQ = PS = SR. If the measure of angle R is 25°, what is the measure of angle QPR?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><polygon points="98.1,97.9 25,185 285,185" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><line x1="98.1" y1="97.9" x2="171.2" y2="185" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="66.2" y1="145.3" x2="57" y2="137.6" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="139.3" y1="137.6" x2="130.1" y2="145.3" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="228.1" y1="179" x2="228.1" y2="191" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><text x="98.1" y="89.9" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">P</text><text x="19" y="205" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">Q</text><text x="289" y="205" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">R</text><text x="171.2" y="205" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">S</text></svg>
explanation: Since PS = SR, triangle PSR is isosceles and angle SPR = angle R = 25°. Angle PSQ is an exterior angle of that triangle, so it is 25 + 25 = 50°. Since PQ = PS, angle PQS = angle PSQ = 50°, which leaves 180 − 100 = 80° for angle QPS. Angle QPR = 80 + 25 = 105°. The choice 80° is only angle QPS, and 50° is angle Q.

stem:
Two sides of a right triangle have lengths 6 and 8. Which of the following could be the length of the third side?

Indicate all such lengths.
explanation: If 6 and 8 are the legs, the hypotenuse is √(36 + 64) = 10. But 8 could itself be the hypotenuse, and then the other leg is √(64 − 36) = √28 = 2√7. Both are possible. Stopping at 10 is the trap: the problem never says which side is the hypotenuse. 2 and 14 come from subtracting or adding the sides.

stem: A regular octagon is formed by cutting four congruent isosceles right triangles from the corners of a square with side length 12, as shown. What is the length of a side of the octagon?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><polygon points="60,15 240,15 240,195 60,195" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><polygon points="112.7,15 187.3,15 240,67.7 240,142.3 187.3,195 112.7,195 60,142.3 60,67.7" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="#dddddd"/><text x="150" y="214" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">12</text></svg>
explanation: Let s be a side of the octagon. Each cut-off triangle has hypotenuse s, so its legs are s/√2. One side of the square is leg + s + leg: s + 2(s/√2) = s(1 + √2) = 12. So s = 12/(1 + √2) = 12(√2 − 1) = 12√2 − 12 ≈ 4.97. The choice 12 − 6√2 ≈ 3.51 is the leg of a cut-off triangle, not the octagon's side, and 4 assumes the square side is split into three equal parts.

stem: A triangle has sides of lengths 8, 15 and x, where x is an integer. If all three angles of the triangle are acute, how many values of x are possible?
explanation: A triangle is acute when the square of its longest side is less than the sum of the squares of the other two. If x is the longest side, x² < 64 + 225 = 289, so x < 17. If 15 is the longest side, 225 < 64 + x², so x² > 161 and x ≥ 13. So x = 13, 14, 15 or 16: 4 values. The triangle inequality alone (7 < x < 23) would allow 15 values, many of which give an obtuse angle.

stem: In the figure, all angles are right angles. What is the perimeter of the figure?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><polygon points="30,20 170,20 170,90 270,90 270,200 30,200" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><text x="150" y="218" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">12</text><text x="16" y="115" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">9</text></svg>
explanation: Slide the two edges of the notch outward: the horizontal notch edge moves up onto the top line and the vertical notch edge moves right onto the right side. The perimeter is therefore the same as that of the full 12-by-9 rectangle, 2(12 + 9) = 42, whatever the size of the notch. The data look insufficient, which tempts test takers to guess a larger number; 108 is the area of the rectangle, not a perimeter.

stem: Triangle T₁ is formed by joining the midpoints of the sides of a triangle with area 80. Triangle T₂ is formed by joining the midpoints of the sides of T₁. What is the area of T₂?
explanation: Joining the midpoints of a triangle's sides creates a triangle similar to the original with ratio ½ (each side is half the side it is parallel to), so its area is (½)² = ¼ of the original. T₁ has area 80/4 = 20 and T₂ has area 20/4 = 5. The choices 40 and 20 halve the area at each step instead of quartering it.

stem: In the figure, the five line segments form a five-pointed star. What is the value of a + b + c + d + e?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><polygon points="150,15 91.2,195.9 245.1,84.1 54.9,84.1 208.8,195.9" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><text x="150" y="53" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">a</text><text x="85.3" y="100" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">b</text><text x="110" y="176" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">c</text><text x="190" y="176" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">d</text><text x="214.7" y="100" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">e</text></svg>
explanation: Look at the small triangle at one tip, say the one containing angle a. Each of its other two angles is an exterior angle of another triangle formed by the star, equal to the sum of two tip angles (for example b + d and c + e). Since the angles of that triangle add up to 180°, a + (b + d) + (c + e) = 180. The result holds for any such star. 36 is one tip of a regular star, and 108 is an interior angle of a regular pentagon.

stem:
The measure of the largest angle of a triangle is exactly 4 times the measure of the smallest angle. Which of the following could be the measure, in degrees, of the smallest angle?

Indicate all such measures.
explanation: If the smallest angle is a, the largest is 4a and the middle one is 180 − 5a. The middle angle must lie between a and 4a: 180 − 5a ≥ a gives a ≤ 30, and 180 − 5a ≤ 4a gives a ≥ 20. So 20, 25 and 30 work (for example 20°, 80°, 80° or 30°, 30°, 120°). With 15 the middle angle would be 105°, larger than 4 × 15 = 60°; with 36 it would be 0°.

stem: Two pentagons are similar. Their perimeters are 15 and 25, and the area of the smaller pentagon is 27. What is the area of the larger pentagon?
explanation: For similar figures, perimeters scale by the length ratio k = 25/15 = 5/3, and areas scale by k² = 25/9. The larger area is 27 × 25/9 = 75. The choice 45 scales the area by k instead of k², and 125 scales it by k³, which is how volumes would scale.

stem: In the figure, ABCD is a square and BCE is an equilateral triangle. What is the measure of angle AEB?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><polygon points="40,50 160,50 160,170 40,170" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><polygon points="160,50 263.9,110 160,170" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><line x1="40" y1="50" x2="263.9" y2="110" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><text x="30" y="44" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">A</text><text x="160" y="42" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">B</text><text x="160" y="190" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">C</text><text x="30" y="188" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">D</text><text x="275.9" y="116" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">E</text></svg>
explanation: AB = BC = BE, so triangle ABE is isosceles with AB = BE. Its vertex angle is ABE = 90° + 60° = 150°, so each base angle is (180 − 150)/2 = 15°. The choice 75° comes from drawing the triangle inside the square, where angle ABE would be 90 − 60 = 30°; 60° is an angle of the equilateral triangle, not of triangle ABE.

stem: Note: Figure not drawn to scale.
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><polygon points="120,30 30,190 270,190" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><text x="120" y="22" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">A</text><text x="20" y="198" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">B</text><text x="280" y="198" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">C</text><text x="63" y="110" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">7</text><text x="207" y="106" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">9</text></svg>
explanation: In any triangle, the larger angle is opposite the longer side. Angle C is opposite AB = 7, and angle B is opposite AC = 9. Since 9 > 7, angle B is larger, whatever the length of BC. Do not try to read the angles from the figure; it is not drawn to scale.

qa: The sum of the measures of the exterior angles of a hexagon, one at each vertex
qb: The sum of the measures of the exterior angles of an octagon, one at each vertex
explanation: Taking one exterior angle at each vertex, the exterior angles of any convex polygon add up to 360°: n(180°) minus the interior sum (n − 2)(180°) is always 360°. So both quantities are 360°. The trap is to think more sides means a larger sum, which is true only for interior angles.

stem: A triangle has sides of lengths 5, 12 and 13.
explanation: Since 5² + 12² = 25 + 144 = 169 = 13², the triangle is a right triangle with legs 5 and 12. Its area is ½ × 5 × 12 = 30, so the quantities are equal. Without spotting the right angle you might think the height is unknown and pick (D).

stem: Note: Figure not drawn to scale.
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><polygon points="40,180 200,180 260,60 100,60" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><text x="120" y="202" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">5</text><text x="230" y="50" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">5</text><text x="58" y="120" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">5</text><text x="244" y="126" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">5</text></svg>
explanation: A quadrilateral with four sides of length 5 is a rhombus. If its angles are right angles it is a square with area 25, but if it leans, its height is less than 5 and its area is less than 25. Both cases fit the information, so the relationship cannot be determined. The figure only looks like a slanted rhombus; it is not drawn to scale, so it cannot settle the question.

stem: Rectangle R has a perimeter of 20 and is not a square.
explanation: The sides add up to 10. Writing them as 5 + d and 5 − d, the area is 25 − d². Because R is not a square, d ≠ 0, so the area is always less than 25. Without the words 'not a square', the answer would be (D), since a 5-by-5 square has area exactly 25.

stem: Two sides of a triangle have lengths 6 and 9.
qa: The length of the third side
explanation: By the triangle inequality the third side is less than 6 + 9 = 15 (and greater than 9 − 6 = 3). It can never reach 15, because then the three segments would lie flat in a line. So Quantity B is always greater.

stem: The hypotenuse of an isosceles right triangle has length 10.
qa: The length of one leg of the triangle
explanation: In an isosceles right triangle the hypotenuse is a leg times √2, so each leg is 10/√2 = 5√2. Since (5√2)² = 50 > 49 = 7², the leg is greater than 7 (about 7.07). Comparing squares avoids rounding √2 too roughly; 1.4 × 5 = 7 would wrongly suggest equality.

stem: In the figure, line ℓ is parallel to line m.
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><line x1="20" y1="60" x2="280" y2="60" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="20" y1="160" x2="280" y2="160" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="196.9" y1="23.7" x2="116.5" y2="196.3" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><text x="272" y="52" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">ℓ</text><text x="272" y="152" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">m</text><text x="144" y="82" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">a°</text><text x="163.4" y="152" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">b°</text></svg>
explanation: Angles a and b lie between the parallel lines on opposite sides of the transversal, so they are alternate interior angles, and alternate interior angles formed by parallel lines are equal. The answer would be (D) only if the lines were not known to be parallel.

stem: Note: Figure not drawn to scale.
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><line x1="20" y1="55" x2="280" y2="70" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="20" y1="165" x2="280" y2="150" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="175" y1="25" x2="135" y2="200" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><text x="272" y="58" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">ℓ</text><text x="272" y="140" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">m</text><text x="188" y="92" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">x°</text><text x="172" y="142" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">y°</text></svg>
explanation: x and y are same-side interior angles, and they add up to 180° only when lines ℓ and m are parallel. Nothing says the lines are parallel, and the figure is not drawn to scale, so the sum could be more than, less than or equal to 180. If the lines tilt toward each other on the right, x + y < 180; if they spread apart, x + y > 180.

stem: The measures of the angles of a triangle are in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3.
qa: The ratio of the length of the longest side to the length of the shortest side
explanation: The angles are 30°, 60° and 90°, so this is a 30°-60°-90° triangle with sides in the ratio 1 : √3 : 2. The longest side (hypotenuse) is twice the shortest side. The trap is to assume the sides are in the same 1 : 2 : 3 ratio as the angles, which would give 3; sides are not proportional to angles.

stem: A square and an equilateral triangle each have a perimeter of 24.
explanation: The square has side 6 and area 36. The triangle has side 8 and area (√3/4) × 8² = 16√3 ≈ 27.7. With equal perimeters, the figure that is 'rounder' (more sides, more regular) encloses more area, so the square wins.

stem: In quadrilateral ABCD, angle A and angle B are right angles.
explanation: The four angles add up to 360°, so C + D = 180°, but nothing fixes how that 180° is split. ABCD could be a rectangle (C = D = 90°) or a right trapezoid with C = 70° and D = 110°, or the other way round. So the relationship cannot be determined.

stem: Note: Figure not drawn to scale.
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><polygon points="60,40 30,190 270,190" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><text x="60" y="32" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">P</text><text x="20" y="198" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">Q</text><text x="280" y="198" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">R</text><text x="74" y="80.3" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">50°</text></svg>
explanation: QR is opposite the 50° angle at P, and PR is opposite angle Q, which is unknown. If angle Q is 70°, then PR is the longer side; if angle Q is 30°, then QR is longer; if angle Q is 50°, they are equal. Only the angle at P is given, so the relationship cannot be determined.

stem: A triangle has sides of lengths 4, 5 and 6.
qa: The measure of the largest angle of the triangle
explanation: The largest angle is opposite the longest side, 6. Compare 6² = 36 with 4² + 5² = 41. Since 36 < 41, the angle is less than 90° (it would be exactly 90° if they were equal, and obtuse if 36 were larger). So Quantity B is greater.

stem: The measures of the angles of a triangle are a°, b° and c°, where a > b > c.
explanation: The three angles average 180/3 = 60°. If the largest angle a were 60 or less, all three would be at most 60 and, since they are not all equal, their sum would be less than 180. So a > 60. Picking an equilateral triangle to test is not allowed here, because the angles must be different.

stem: Note: Figure not drawn to scale.
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><polygon points="30,180 210,180 270,70 90,70" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><text x="120" y="202" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">8</text><text x="46" y="125" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">5</text></svg>
explanation: The area is the base 8 times the height. The height is at most the slanted side 5, and equals 5 only when the parallelogram is a rectangle. So the area is 40 for a rectangle and less than 40 otherwise. Since the figure is not drawn to scale, its angles cannot be assumed, and the relationship cannot be determined.

stem: A right triangle has a hypotenuse of length 10 and one leg of length 6.
qa: The length of the other leg
explanation: The other leg is √(10² − 6²) = √64 = 8, which is greater than 7. This is the 3-4-5 triangle scaled by 2. A hurried reader may add the squares (√136) or subtract the lengths (4); both are mistakes, but here the subtraction slip would flip the answer.

stem: The lengths of the sides of a triangle are integers, and the perimeter of the triangle is 12.
qa: The length of the longest side
explanation: Any side must be shorter than the sum of the other two, which is 12 minus that side. So each side is less than 12/2 = 6. The possible triangles are 2-5-5, 3-4-5 and 4-4-4, with longest side 5, 5 or 4. Sides 6, 5, 1 fail because 5 + 1 = 6 is not greater than 6.

stem:
In triangle ABC, D is a point on BC with BD = DC.

Note: Figure not drawn to scale.
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><polygon points="90,30 30,190 270,190" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><line x1="90" y1="30" x2="150" y2="190" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="90" y1="184" x2="90" y2="196" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="210" y1="184" x2="210" y2="196" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><text x="90" y="22" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">A</text><text x="20" y="198" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">B</text><text x="280" y="198" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">C</text><text x="150" y="210" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">D</text></svg>
explanation: Triangles ABD and ADC have equal bases BD = DC, and they share the same height: the perpendicular distance from A to line BC. So their areas are equal, whatever the shape of triangle ABC. The figure makes ABD look smaller, but it is not drawn to scale and the shape does not matter anyway.

stem: The sum of the measures of the interior angles of a convex polygon is 1,080°.
qa: The number of sides of the polygon
qb: The number of diagonals of a pentagon
explanation: From (n − 2) × 180 = 1,080, n − 2 = 6 and n = 8. A pentagon has 5 × (5 − 3)/2 = 5 diagonals. So Quantity A, 8, is greater. Count diagonals with n(n − 3)/2; using n(n − 1)/2 = 10 for the pentagon counts its sides too and would wrongly make B larger.

stem: Two angles are supplementary, and one of them measures 35°. What is the measure of the other angle?
explanation: Supplementary angles add up to 180°, so the other angle is 180 − 35 = 145°. The choice 55° is the complement (angles adding up to 90°), and 325° subtracts from 360°.

stem: In the triangle shown, what is the value of x?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><polygon points="193.7,21.3 30,185 270,185" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><text x="65.1" y="175.5" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">45°</text><text x="243" y="172.8" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">65°</text><text x="188.5" y="55.9" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">x°</text></svg>
explanation: The angles of a triangle add up to 180°, so x = 180 − 45 − 65 = 70. The choice 110 is 45 + 65, which would be the exterior angle at the top vertex, not the interior angle x.

stem: A rectangular garden is 7 meters wide and 12 meters long. How many meters of fencing are needed to go once around the garden?
explanation: The fencing goes around the edge, so it equals the perimeter: 2 × (7 + 12) = 38 meters. Multiplying 7 × 12 = 84 gives the area, which measures the ground inside, not the edge.

qa: The measure of each interior angle of an equilateral triangle
explanation: An equilateral triangle has three equal angles that add up to 180°, so each one is 180/3 = 60°. The quantities are equal.

stem: A square has sides of length 5.
explanation: The perimeter is 4 × 5 = 20 and the area is 5 × 5 = 25, so B is greater. Note that this depends on the side length: for a square with side 4 the two would be equal (16 and 16), and for a smaller square the perimeter would be larger.

stem: The legs of a right triangle have lengths 5 and 12. What is the length of the hypotenuse?
explanation: By the Pythagorean theorem, the hypotenuse is √(5² + 12²) = √(25 + 144) = √169 = 13. The choice 17 simply adds the legs, which the triangle inequality rules out: the hypotenuse must be shorter than 5 + 12.

stem: Note: Figure not drawn to scale.
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><line x1="20" y1="160" x2="280" y2="160" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="150" y1="160" x2="186.2" y2="24.8" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><text x="124.3" y="129.4" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">x°</text><text x="186.9" y="134.2" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">y°</text></svg>
explanation: The two angles together form a straight angle, so x + y = 180. That is all we know: x = 100 and y = 80 fit, and so do x = 80 and y = 100, or 90 and 90. The figure makes x look larger, but it is not drawn to scale, so the relationship cannot be determined.

stem: A triangle has a base of 10 centimeters and a height of 7 centimeters. What is its area, in square centimeters?
explanation: The area of a triangle is ½ × base × height = ½ × 10 × 7 = 35 square centimeters. The choice 70 forgets the ½ and is the area of a 10-by-7 rectangle.

stem:
In the pentagon shown, what is the value of x?

Note: Figure not drawn to scale.
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><polygon points="150,25 265,95 230,195 70,200 30,90" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><text x="149.2" y="62" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">95°</text><text x="234.9" y="110.8" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">105°</text><text x="211.1" y="174.2" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">100°</text><text x="87.9" y="178.5" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">110°</text><text x="59.9" y="106.4" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">x°</text></svg>
explanation: The interior angles of a pentagon add up to (5 − 2) × 180 = 540°. The four given angles add up to 95 + 105 + 100 + 110 = 410°, so x = 540 − 410 = 130. The choice 108 is the angle of a regular pentagon, which does not apply because these angles are unequal; 50 comes from using 460°.

stem:
Which of the following could be the measure, in degrees, of an exterior angle of a regular polygon?

Indicate all such measures.
explanation: The exterior angles of a regular n-sided polygon are each 360/n, so a measure works only if 360 divided by it is a whole number of at least 3. 15 gives 24 sides, 40 gives 9 and 72 gives 5. For 25, 50 and 100, 360 divided by the angle is 14.4, 7.2 and 3.6, which are not whole numbers.

stem: In triangle ABC, AB = AC and the measure of angle A is 50°.
explanation: Since AB = AC, the angles opposite those sides, B and C, are equal. They share 180 − 50 = 130°, so angle B = 65°, which is greater than 50°. Mixing up which angles are equal (thinking angle B equals angle A) leads to (C).

stem: The figure shows a rectangle with sides 6 and 8 and one diagonal.
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><polygon points="50,40 250,40 250,190 50,190" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><line x1="50" y1="40" x2="250" y2="190" stroke="black" stroke-width="2"/><text x="150" y="210" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">8</text><text x="36" y="120" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">6</text></svg>
explanation: The diagonal is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs 6 and 8, so it is √(36 + 64) = 10. That is less than 14, which is the sum 6 + 8. Walking along two sides is always longer than cutting across.

stem: At the same time of day, a person 1.6 meters tall casts a shadow 2 meters long and a tree casts a shadow 15 meters long. How tall, in meters, is the tree?
explanation: The sun's rays make similar right triangles, so height/shadow is the same for both: 1.6/2 = h/15, so h = 15 × 0.8 = 12 meters. The choice 18.75 flips the ratio (15 × 2/1.6), and 13 is 15 − 2, which treats the relationship as a difference rather than a ratio.

stem: A regular hexagon has a perimeter of 36. What is the length of its longest diagonal?
explanation: Each side is 36/6 = 6. A regular hexagon splits into six equilateral triangles meeting at the center, and the longest diagonal passes through the center across two of them, so it is 2 × 6 = 12. A shorter diagonal, joining vertices two apart, is 6√3 ≈ 10.4.

stem: A triangle has sides of lengths 3, 8 and x.
explanation: By the triangle inequality, x must be greater than 8 − 3 = 5 and less than 8 + 3 = 11. So x > 5 always. If x were exactly 5, the sides 3 and 5 would add up to exactly 8 and the triangle would collapse into a line segment.

stem: What is the area of the trapezoid shown?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><polygon points="40,180 260,180 172,92 40,92" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><polyline points="50,180 50,170 40,170" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><polyline points="40,102 50,102 50,92" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><text x="150" y="202" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">10</text><text x="106" y="84" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">6</text><text x="26" y="141" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">4</text></svg>
explanation: The left side is perpendicular to both bases, so it is the height, 4. The area of a trapezoid is the average of the bases times the height: (6 + 10)/2 × 4 = 32. The choices 24 and 40 use only one base (6 × 4 or 10 × 4).

stem: The measures of the angles of a triangle are x°, 2x° and 3x°.
explanation: The angles add up to 180, so 6x = 180 and x = 30. Then 3x = 90: the triangle is a 30°-60°-90° right triangle, and the quantities are equal.

stem: A right triangle has a hypotenuse of length 13 and an area of 30. What is the perimeter of the triangle?
explanation: If the legs are a and b, then ab/2 = 30 so ab = 60, and a² + b² = 169. Then (a + b)² = 169 + 2(60) = 289, so a + b = 17 and the perimeter is 17 + 13 = 30. The choice 17 is only the sum of the legs, and 43 adds the area to the hypotenuse.

stem:
A triangle has sides of lengths 5, 7 and x, where x is an integer, and one of its angles is obtuse. Which of the following could be the value of x?

Indicate all such values.
explanation: A triangle is obtuse when the square of its longest side exceeds the sum of the squares of the other two. If x is the longest side, x² > 25 + 49 = 74, so x ≥ 9; with x < 12 from the triangle inequality, 9 and 11 work. If 7 is the longest side, 49 > 25 + x², so x² < 24 and x ≤ 4; with x > 2, 3 and 4 work. Missing this second case is the main trap.

stem:
In triangle ABC, AB > BC.

Note: Figure not drawn to scale.
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><polygon points="110,35 30,190 270,190" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><text x="110" y="27" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">A</text><text x="20" y="198" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">B</text><text x="280" y="198" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">C</text></svg>
explanation: In a triangle the longer side is opposite the larger angle. AB is opposite angle C and BC is opposite angle A, so AB > BC means angle C > angle A. The figure suggests otherwise, but it is not drawn to scale; the trap is matching each side with an angle at one of its own endpoints.

stem: A triangle has sides of lengths 6, 8 and x, where 10 < x < 14.
explanation: Treat 6 as the base hinged to the side 8. The area is ½ × 6 × (height from the far end of the 8 side), and that height is at most 8, reaching 8 only when the angle between the sides is 90°, which happens when x = 10. Because x > 10, the angle is obtuse, the height is less than 8 and the area is less than ½ × 6 × 8 = 24.

stem: An isosceles triangle has a perimeter of 20, and one of its sides has length 8.
explanation: The side of length 8 could be one of the two equal sides (sides 8, 8, 4) or the base (sides 6, 6, 8). For 8, 8, 4 the height to the base is √(64 − 4) = √60, giving area 2√60 ≈ 15.5 < 16. For 6, 6, 8 the height is √(36 − 16) = √20, giving area 4√20 ≈ 17.9 > 16. Both triangles fit, so the relationship cannot be determined.

stem: The figure shows a square with side length 7. Each vertex of the shaded square lies on a side of the larger square and divides that side into segments of lengths 3 and 4, as shown for the top side. What is the area of the shaded square?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><polygon points="60,20 242,20 242,202 60,202" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><polygon points="138,20 242,98 164,202 60,124" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="#dddddd"/><text x="99" y="14" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">3</text><text x="190" y="14" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">4</text></svg>
explanation: The four unshaded corner triangles are right triangles with legs 3 and 4, each with area 6. The shaded area is 49 − 4 × 6 = 25. Equivalently, each side of the shaded square is the hypotenuse √(3² + 4²) = 5, so its area is 25. The choices 43, 37 and 31 remove only one, two or three of the corner triangles.

stem: Each interior angle of a regular polygon is 100° greater than each exterior angle. How many sides does the polygon have?
explanation: An interior angle i and its exterior angle e satisfy i + e = 180 and, here, i − e = 100. Subtracting gives 2e = 80, so e = 40°, and the number of sides is 360/40 = 9. Dividing 360 by 100 or by the interior angle 140 does not give a whole number, a sign that the setup is off.

stem: In triangle ABC, AB = AC = 10 and BC = 12. What is the length of the altitude from C to side AB, shown as a dashed segment?
figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 220"><polygon points="148,41 40,185 256,185" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><line x1="256" y1="185" x2="117.8" y2="81.3" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/><polyline points="125,86.7 130.4,79.5 123.2,74.1" stroke="black" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><text x="80" y="113" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">10</text><text x="216" y="113" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">10</text><text x="148" y="207" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">12</text><text x="148" y="33" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">A</text><text x="30" y="193" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">B</text><text x="266" y="193" font-size="16" font-family="sans-serif" text-anchor="middle">C</text></svg>
explanation: First find the area using the altitude from A to BC: it splits BC into halves of 6, so its length is √(100 − 36) = 8 and the area is ½ × 12 × 8 = 48. The same area equals ½ × AB × h, so ½ × 10 × h = 48 and h = 9.6. The choice 8 is the altitude to BC, not to AB.
